searchText: Hello Eth Devs, I come in peace I am a Dev for BCHN, the leading fullnode software for Bitcoin Cash (BCH). I am doing performance work, and in the middle of doing research on how other fullnode software implemented their network code I have done a write-up on geth, and am looking to check if it is factually correct. Is this the right avenue? My write-up: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/i-have-written-a-short-writeup-of-how-geths-network-processing-works-and-im-looking-for-someone-to-verify-that-it-is-indeed-correct/8994 Thank you in advance I hope it's not impolite to tag a geth Dev <@360491619402776577> Looks good to me I appreciate this immensely Btw something that BCH might consider: https://medium.com/@m.vanderwijden1/faster-block-propagation-in-blockchain-networks-2ad0ab3097a3 It's not really useful in ethereum since blocks are small, but might make sense with the big blocks of BCH. It can significantly reduce the time needed to propagate a block, while still being resilient against DDOS attacks I'll definitely have an in-depth read, and point it out to others It makes a lot of sense to have blocks forwarded soon by trusted peers BCHN people are noting that BCHN has inherited the CompactBlocks scheme from Core via ABC (https://bitcoincore.org/en/2016/06/07/compact-blocks-faq/), which does a version of what you describe. To the best of my understanding, only BitcoinUnlimited implements it correctly, as BCHN (and Core) cannot forward missing transactions until it is done processingg the block, by virtue of the network being singlethreaded, making the scheme moot (unless the mempools are already in sync, which is a hard assumption). This singlethreadedness is what I wish to tackle in the coming months. I'll end non-Eth talk now. Thank you a lot! Also, is Mr Popovitch around?
